brief: Goldman's industrials/A&D sales desk opens with morning macro color: Brazil's Bolsonaro surprise lead lifts local markets, Spain's snap-election call pressures the Euro to 17-month lows, and French political uncertainty weighs on French equities. Aerospace stocks resemble March/April (elevated jet fuel, travel-slowdown fears), but seven to eight further months into the Middle East conflict mean time is now working against the growth outlook rather than allowing adjustment, and OEM-side length (Boeing and the supply chain) has proven frustrating. More-owned names include BA, RBC, CRS, ATI and DPC, with warming interest in HONA. WWD and HWM are debated. TDG, HEI and TXT are underowned. Defense primes have underperformed even during risk-off periods. A midterm blue wave and SPCX lockup expirations add overhangs, with sentiment split: LMT and GD positive, RTX mixed, NOC and LHX negative. Separately, GS Eco expects most S&P 500 companies to beat again in Q3 as median-stock EPS growth decelerates to 9% from 14%, with AI beneficiaries driving over half of index EPS growth on 116% hyperscaler capex growth. DAL, reporting Friday, guided full-year EPS of $6.50-7.50 against a Street estimate of $5.89. RPM, reporting Tuesday, shows unusually low sentiment despite consensus EBITDA growth sitting at its guidance midpoint.
